title: OocystMeter segments malaria oocysts and reveals clustering in the mosquito midgut
summary: A fine-tuned Mask R-CNN, trained on 11,178 expert-annotated Plasmodium falciparum oocysts in Anopheles gambiae midguts, matched human parasitologists (Spearman 0.998 for counts, 0.978 for sizes). Tool-assisted annotations with spatial analysis showed non-random oocyst clustering at short spatial scales in infections of 4-74 oocysts per midgut, with no consistent anatomical region explaining it. This is mainly a tool paper read at abstract level, and clustering statistics were not reviewed.
ai_technology: Fine-tuned Mask R-CNN instance segmentation of oocysts giving counts, sizes and spatial coordinates

evidence.tested: Segmentation agreement with expert parasitologists; spatial analysis of tool-assisted annotations.
evidence.unknown: Clustering statistics and mechanism of the pattern. Full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Segmented oocysts to enable counting, sizing and spatial analysis.
